title: Rahul Gandhi Names Modi, Shah Over Delhi Protest Crackdown, Calls Supreme Court March
excerpt: The Congress leader accused police and BJP workers of beating peaceful protesters, announced a Monday march to the Supreme Court over voter-roll revision — and the BJP hit straight back.
body:
• Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday accused police and BJP workers of beating peaceful young protesters in Delhi, calling it "not the India we want", and announced a march to the Supreme Court on Monday, October 12.
  • The march — expected to draw opposition parties and civil society groups — will submit a memorandum to Chief Justice Surya Kant demanding an end to alleged "vote chori", a halt to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, and the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
  • Gandhi named Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah, NSA Ajit Doval and RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, saying they "cannot silence India's voice" and "will have to step aside".
  • The BJP hit back: advocate Karuna Sagar accused the INDIA bloc and the Cockroach Janata Party of "creating a ruckus and trying to seize the National Capital"; Delhi CM Rekha Gupta accused Congress, AAP, the Left and the CJP of chaos and praised Delhi Police; Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar mocked the opposition's sporadic protests.

"Daro mat" — a call to march on the Supreme Court

In a post on Sunday, Rahul Gandhi said the protesters who came out in Delhi the previous day had come "with love in their hearts, not hatred or anger" and accused the authorities of trying to suppress their voices. Announcing Monday's march, he said participants would carry a memorandum to the Chief Justice demanding an end to alleged electoral malpractice, a halt to the SIR exercise and the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=xqLlLBDkf3k

"Youth, all opposition parties, civil society groups, all those who believe in democracy and stand by the Constitution of India, will walk with us," he said, adding that the march would unite people across party, gender, caste, community and state lines. He ended the message: "Daro mat. Tomorrow, all of India will march to the Supreme Court."

"Yesterday, the nation's young came out in Delhi to peacefully protest. They came with love in their hearts, not hatred or anger. They were beaten, both by cops and BJP goons. This is not the India we want."

— Rahul Gandhi, Congress leader

What triggered the confrontation

The announcement came a day after a sweeping security crackdown as police blocked Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) supporters and opposition leaders from reaching Jantar Mantar on Saturday. More than 7,000 protesters were detained — including CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, and former chief ministers Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar — as Times of India. over 30,000 police and paramilitary personnel were deployed across the capital.

https://x.com/RahulGandhi/status/2109271519373545893

Section 133 of the BNSS has been imposed across several areas of Delhi, barring unauthorised gatherings. The CJP leaders, released after being produced before an executive magistrate, have vowed to take the agitation nationwide until accountability is secured. (The Videshi's earlier coverage: CJP protest crackdown and the Supreme Court's Sunday sitting on the detentions.)

Context & Background

At the centre of the dispute is the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls — a verification drive the Commission says cleans the lists, but which the CJP and the opposition allege is being used to disenfranchise voters. The demand for CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation has now been taken up by the Congress leadership itself, moving the fight from a fringe party's agitation to the mainstream opposition's campaign. Delhi Police answers to the Union Home Ministry, not the elected Delhi government — which is why Gandhi's attack lands squarely on Modi and Shah.

The BJP hits back

The opposition's allegations drew a sharp counter from the BJP. BJP leader and advocate Karuna Sagar said the INDIA bloc and the CJP had "created a ruckus and tried to seize the National Capital." Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta accused Congress, AAP, Left parties and the CJP of creating chaos during the protests and praised Delhi Police for handling the situation and ensuring public safety. Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar dismissed the protests, saying the opposition "occasionally makes its presence felt, much like a cockroach crawling across one's back."

The government line is that the detentions were preventive and necessary to maintain public order in the capital — a claim the opposition, led by Gandhi, rejects as a pretext for silencing dissent.

What's Next

Monday's march to the Supreme Court is the immediate flashpoint. The opposition wants to submit its memorandum directly to Chief Justice Surya Kant — but the CJI has already declined a meeting request from Rahul Gandhi and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on the SIR and police-action issues, PTI reported, citing sources, in a Mint report. Whether authorities permit Monday's assembly — or whether the capital sees another round of metro restrictions and mass detentions — will be the test of whether this confrontation escalates further.
